data.title: Middle East Eye: Cop31 ends in failure as countries reject climate deal over fossil fuels
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Cop31 ends in failure as countries reject climate deal over fossil fuels
The United Nations climate summit in Turkey became the longest-ever UN climate conference on Sunday as negotiations over a final agreement descended into deadlock, with the European Union and several other countries formally rejecting the proposed text.
The talks in Antalya, known as Cop31, continued more than 44 hours beyond their scheduled Friday conclusion, surpassing the previous record set by Cop25 in Madrid in 2019.
The latest draft, presented by the Turkish and Australian presidencies in an attempt to bridge divisions between countries, failed to secure consensus over its omission of explicit references to fossil fuels and disagreements over climate finance.
At the closing plenary, Cop31 President Murat Kurum acknowledged that countries had failed to agree on the proposed document.
“We have done our utmost. Ultimately, we have not imposed this text on anyone, nor have we issued an ultimatum such as a ‘take it or leave it’ demand,” Kurum said.
This is a developing story. We'll bring more updates shortly.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Saudi Arabia, Qatar join condemnation of Iran attack on Bahrain
data.author: Daniel Tester
data.summary:
Saudi Arabia, Qatar join condemnation of Iran attack on Bahrain
Saudi Arabia and Qatar have joined the UAE in condemning Iran's attack on Bahrain earlier on Sunday.
In a statement posted on X, Qatar's foreign ministry expressed its "categorical rejection of attacks on economic facilities, civilian objects and civilians, and affirms that the continuation of these attacks represents a dangerous escalation that threatens the region’s security and stability”.
Saudi Arabia, meanwhile, said it "affirms its full solidarity with Bahrain in all measures it takes to protect its security and stability", accusing Tehran of "undermining regional security and stability”.
Iran attacked US military bases in both Qatar and Saudi Arabia, along with Bahrain, Kuwait, the UAE, Oman, Iraq and Jordan throughout the first months of the war, which began in late February. But such attacks have lulled since April amid ceasefire negotiations between Washington and Tehran.

Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks
Representatives from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and the party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar, met on Sunday to discuss forming a unity government, Haaretz is reporting.
The meeting follows earlier talks last Sunday after nearly a month of deadlock in the Israeli Knesset since October's election, which saw no party gain an overall majority. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have so far failed to negotiate a viable coalition government alongside smaller parties.
Absent from Sunday's meeting were representatives of Naftali Bennett's Together party, which received the third-largest vote share and attended the previous round of talks.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.
Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.
"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.
The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported.
According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island.
Both vessels reportedly stopped moving.
Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker.
The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses".
UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman.
It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
Bahrain said on Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed earlier in November.
"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.
"His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition."
Residents had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco, AFP reported.
In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the IRGC said they had attacked US Patriot air defence systems with missiles and drones at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Bahrain's foreign ministry dismissed the IRGC's account, saying the site hit was purely civilian and industrial, calling the attack a direct danger to civilians and a violation of the kingdom's sovereignty.
Bahrain's neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday also condemned Tehran for its attacks on Gulf countries.
The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X "the strongest condemnation and denunciation... of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain".

data.title: Middle East Eye: Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher, as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.
"A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday.
State television broadcast footage of Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's Aerospace Force, touring an underground missile base.
The two commanders were shown riding on top of a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.
"The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," Vahidi said.
"Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi.
During the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted the country's missile capabilities and hit its nuclear sites for a second time, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.
Earlier this month, the IRGC unveiled what it described as new underground "missile cities" housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.
“The latest round of coalition talks… has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,” the two parties said in a joint statement.
“A follow-up meeting will be held,” they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with the possibility of a 14‑day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.
His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra‑Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids and attacks across the occupied West Bank on Sunday, injuring and detaining Palestinians, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. The attacks come amid a sharp escalation in settler violence in the territory.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages, setting fire to 12 vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
The attacks targeted Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, in the Ramallah and al-Bireh governorate.
Near Hizma, north-east of Jerusalem, Israeli forces fired live ammunition at Palestinian workers trying to cross the separation wall into the city, wounding several of them, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.
Around 18 workers were detained, and video footage showed one of them being severely beaten.
The Palestine Red Crescent said it treated two people who were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces and falling from the wall. Israeli forces later closed the entrances to Hizma and forced shops to shut.
In al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, several Palestinians were injured by flying glass when settlers attacked vehicles on Sunday evening, the head of the village council, Amin Abu Alia, told Wafa.
Abu Alia said settlers, protected by Israeli forces, gathered at the village entrances and prevented residents from entering or leaving. He added that Israeli forces detained several Palestinians, and that there was no information so far on their fate or whereabouts.
Many Palestinian residents were also left stranded in the neighbouring village of Abu Falah, unable to return home.
South of Jenin, Israeli forces raided the towns of Anza, Jaba', Arraba and Ya'bad. Video footage showed Palestinian man severely beaten by Israeli soldiers inside his house in Ya'bad.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks by settlers in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism", accusing far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir of fuelling violence against Palestinians.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages near Ramallah, setting fire to vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, described the attacks as "Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word" and called on the government and security establishment to take tougher action against violent settlers.
"The acts of sabotage carried out by extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes undermine regional stability, endanger lives and seriously harm Israel's national security and foreign relations," he wrote on X.
Opposition leader Yair Lapid also condemned the attacks, calling them "Jewish terrorism" caused by government negligence.
"Jewish terrorism is the product of criminal negligence on the part of the Israeli government," Lapid said. "By remaining silent, government ministers are deliberately encouraging these pogroms."
"When we form a government, we will tackle this terrorism and restore governance, law and order," he added.
In the United States, Democratic Congressman Josh Gottheimer condemned the attacks and called for accountability.
"These incidents warrant a full and thorough investigation," Gottheimer wrote on X, adding that vigilante justice had "no place" in society.
Israeli police said they had opened investigations into arson, vandalism and property damage.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
Israeli forces detonated explosives to destroy structures on the outskirts of Qantara in southern Lebanon, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported.
Earlier on Sunday, Israeli forces set off a massive explosion in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, followed by another in Kfar Tibnit, according to NNA.
The blasts could be heard across much of southern Lebanon.
Residents of Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Zawtar held two separate protests against the Lebanese government's "silence" over Israel's occupation of areas up to the Litani River, which began in March, according to NNA.
Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said he would not accept congratulations on Lebanon's Independence Day, which falls on 22 November, in solidarity with residents of the occupied southern border villages.
In a statement, Berri described this year's independence as "incomplete and unfulfilled".
He said it would be complete only once Lebanese territory was liberated and official and popular positions were united again.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages.
Footage from Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik on Sunday shows burnt-out cars and graffiti reading "Death to Arabs" and "Revenge" painted on walls. Residents said settlers attacked their villages while families were asleep, leaving multiple vehicles destroyed.
"We were sleeping and not expecting that herds of settlers will attack our homes while people are sleeping, we never expected this," said Muneer Alkhatib, a resident of Deir Abu Mashal.
Another resident, Montaser Almalki, said the attackers came from a nearby settler outpost and warned that his family could have been caught in a fire had they not woken up.
The attacks took place across several locations in the occupied West Bank. They were condemned by Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who described them as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging the violence.

data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The minister told lawmakers that the deployment was not indirect military participation in the conflict, but instead cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

A Saudi attack on Yemen's key port city of Hodeida killed at least four people and injured 18 others, according to Houthi-affiliated media.
The strike reportedly targeted a building belonging to Yemen's Public Telecommunications Corporation.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
data.author: Mera Aladam
data.summary:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections.
"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his platform Truth Social.
Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".
"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed.
Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".
In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"
